name: Green tea extract and EGCG
short: Concentrated green tea extracts taken in large doses, especially when fasting, have been linked to liver injury in case reports and trials; brewed tea was not.
text: A systematic review of adverse event data from 159 human intervention studies found that concentrated, catechin-rich green tea preparations caused liver adverse events in a dose-dependent manner when taken as large bolus doses, but not when consumed as brewed tea or in beverages or food. A United States Pharmacopeia review reported case reports linking liver injury to EGCG intakes starting from 140 mg/day, with substantial differences in individual susceptibility, and found that repeated bolus doses taken while fasting markedly increase EGCG absorption. In a small trial in 39 premenopausal women, 800 mg EGCG daily, alone or with an ovarian stimulator, caused no signs of drug-induced liver injury. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
